description.narrative: Owing to public's limited awareness and concern about autism, autism spectrum disorder and difficulties faced by children with autistic, autism spectrum disorder and their families, Nghe An National Fund for Vietnamese Children decided to implement awareness raising activities series for the community about autism and autisms spectrum disorder, in parallel, organize activities to support families of children diagnosed with autism or autisms spectrum disorder. Ultimately, the project aims to help childrenwith autism to be protected by law with realistic, appropriate and fair policies; have accessed and benefited from national public health services, education and welfare policies. Its long-term goals, in fact, focuses on building a core team at grass-rootlevels with team members are officials including officials of cultural and social departments, preschool teachers, health workers and people working in centersfor special education. They are well-equipped with knowledge and skills to support children with autism to access public health services, education and welfare. The project areas cover 5 communes of Nghe An, including Anh Son, Dien Chau, Quynh Luu, Nghi Loc and Do Luong. Overall, it is expected to have 154 socio-cultural officials, 154 health workers from 154 wards and communes in the projectarea with increased awareness of autism spectrum disorder in children; about 200 preschools have staff who are trained and equippedwith knowledge and skills to recognize symptoms and support children; all children with autism are supported to access and get benefited from health care, education, and welfare systems.

participating-org.narrative: National Fund for Vietnamese Children Nghe An Province was established in 2002, under the Provincial Committee for Population, Family and Children. The Fund connects domestic and foreign agencies, organizations and individuals, and international aid, following its vision to ensure children have their basic rights. After more than 21 years of operation, it has mobilized nearly 200 billion VND to support more than 430,000 children with extremely difficult circumstances in the province, providing counseling, therapy, early diagnosis and intervention for more than 27,000 children with autism. On daily average, it receives 100 children for rehabilitation and autism treatment at its units (providing support to children and their families). Most of the childrenafter treatment have made significant progress in both cognitive development and mobility. The Fund was awarded the third-class Labor Medal in 2010. It also received many certificates of merit from relevant agencies and departments for contributions to the work of children care and protection with a core team having a great amount of experience in project implementation and management.
